title: Build the Enterprise Facilities agent on Microsoft Azure

layers.title: Foundation Models
layers.objective: Call a foundation model from code the way every other layer will: a chat turn, a tool-calling turn and an embedding.
learn: One request shape for chat; tool calling: the model asks, your code runs the tool
Embeddings turn text into vectors for search
The model catalogue versus the model id your code uses
build: List the chat and embed deployments through ARM.
embeddings.create (1536 dimensions, and dimensions=256).
chat.completions: a chat turn through your deployment name.
chat.completions with a function tool, and with stream=True.
An unknown deployment answers 404 DeploymentNotFound; the content filter refuses a violent prompt (chapter 11).
simplified: Answers come from one small local open model, not GPT; quality is far lower.
Deployments are mapped to the local models.

code.text:
from openai import AzureOpenAI
client = AzureOpenAI(azure_endpoint=ENDPOINT, api_key=KEY, api_version="2024-06-01")
r = client.chat.completions.create(model="chat",   # your deployment name
                                   messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}])
print(r.choices[0].message.content)

layers.outcome: A model client any layer can import: chat, tool calling and embeddings

layers.title: Agent Runtime
layers.objective: Host a supervisor agent that routes work to Facilities, Maintenance and Analytics sub-agents, one isolated session at a time.
learn: Supervisor and sub-agents: plan, route, synthesise
The agent harness: step, token and cost budgets, checkpoints, timeouts, a kill switch
Session isolation: separate state per session
build: Create the supervisor and Facilities, Maintenance and Analytics agents with azure-ai-agents.
Run the supervisor on a thread.
Create the Container Apps environment and the facilities-supervisor app through ARM.
POST /query on the ingress: the LangGraph supervisor runs the sub-agents in the container.
simplified: Azure has no hosted-agent runtime like AgentCore Runtime or Vertex Agent Engine: this layer is assembled (agents plus a container), and says so.
layers.native: Assembled: Foundry Agents plus a container host.
layers.outcome: A supervisor agent and three sub-agents answering in isolated sessions

layers.title: Tools
layers.objective: Build the tools the agents call: read-only lookups first, then write tools that sit behind approval.
learn: A tool is a function with a clear input and output contract
Read-only tools versus approval-gated write tools
Tool code never trusts its caller
build: Seed assets and work orders in Table storage.
ARM plan and site, then zip deploy the four functions.
ARM list_functions and list_host_keys (the key authorises calls).
Invoke kb-search (AI Search from inside the function).
Invoke asset-status (Table read from inside the function).
simplified: Functions run in a simulator sandbox; scale-out, plans and cold starts are not modelled.
layers.outcome: Read-only and approval-gated tools your agents can call

layers.title: Knowledge Pipeline
layers.objective: Turn documents into searchable knowledge, and re-index automatically when a new document lands.
learn: Chunking and why chunk size matters
Embeddings and vector search
Event-driven ingestion: storage event, function, index job
build: Create the docs container and upload the four SOP documents.
AI Search: blob data source and indexer fill facilities-kb.
Check all four documents are searchable.
Deploy an ingest function that runs the indexer.
Event Grid system topic on the storage account with an AzureFunction subscription: a new blob is re-ingested automatically.
simplified: Embeddings come from a small local model; the search engine is a lightweight one behind the same API.
layers.outcome: Documents flowing into a searchable knowledge base, re-indexed on every upload

layers.title: Knowledge Search (RAG)
layers.objective: Retrieve the right passages for a question, rank them, and keep the source so answers can cite it.
learn: Vector, keyword and hybrid retrieval
Reranking
Why sources must travel with results
build: create_or_update_index with text, vector and semantic configuration.
Embed the documents and merge the vectors.
BM25 search: the boiler SOP ranks first; the HVAC manual ranks first for an AHU question.
Vector query, then hybrid query (text plus vector, RRF).
Semantic ranker returns a reranker score; every result carries its source name.
simplified: Ranking depends on a small local embedding model; the semantic ranker is simplified.
layers.outcome: Ranked retrieval that keeps the source of every passage

layers.title: Response Generation
layers.objective: Answer in plain language from the retrieved documents, with citations, and filter sensitive data out before the user sees it.
learn: Grounding: answer only from retrieved text
Citations and how to check them
Output guardrails: sensitive-data masking and policy filters
build: Generate a grounded answer from AI Search results and cite them.
Content Safety on the answer: a harmful completion is flagged, the clean answer passes.
Assistants: a vector store and file_search with file_citation annotations.
On Your Data: chat grounded on the AI Search index returns citations.
simplified: Content Safety is a deterministic filter set, not Microsoft's trained classifiers.
Answer quality is that of a small local model.
layers.outcome: Grounded answers with citations and sensitive data masked

layers.title: Agent Memory
layers.objective: Give the agent memory: short-term events inside a session and long-term facts it can retrieve later.
learn: Short-term memory is the events of one session
Long-term memory outlives a session
Scope memory per user and tenant; mind retention and poisoning
build: Create a thread with metadata and two user messages (short-term memory).
GET messages returns the history in order; update and retrieve thread metadata.
A run recalls a fact from earlier in the thread.
Long-term: store a user fact in Table storage; a new session recalls it.
Confirm Azure has no managed long-term memory API.
checks: a fact is recalled in a new session
simplified: Azure has NO managed long-term memory API (unlike AgentCore Memory and Vertex Memory Bank): long-term memory here is an application pattern you write yourself.
layers.native: Application pattern: Azure has no managed long-term memory.
layers.outcome: Short-term session memory and retrievable long-term facts

layers.title: Agent Gateway
layers.objective: Put one governed door in front of the tools: a tool catalogue, a policy check on every call and a rate limit.
learn: Tool catalogue over MCP
Policy on every tool call: identity, role, attributes
Throttling, schema validation and audit with the user identity
build: Create the tool catalogue: an API with three operations.
Call a read-only tool (asset-status) through the gateway with a subscription key.
Add an operation policy (rate-limit).
Add a policy expression that denies the write tool without an approval id.
Expose tools/list and tools/call as a JSON-RPC MCP API.
checks: write tool denied without an approval id
simplified: There is no Cedar equivalent on Azure: the substitute is APIM policy expressions (choose/when).
layers.native: No Cedar on Azure: APIM policy expressions.
layers.outcome: One governed gateway with a tool catalogue and a read-only policy

layers.title: Actions and Approval
layers.objective: Make write actions safe: park the action for a human, record every decision, and only then execute.
learn: Risk levels: low auto-approves, medium and high need a human
Durable approval state and a callback
An approval ledger as the system of record; idempotency
build: The agent writes a PENDING ledger row and sends the request to the work-order-approval topic.
The approver reads the approver-inbox subscription (AMQP).
The approval-decision function rejects an unauthorised approver and records APPROVED or REJECTED (ETag-conditional).
The waiting caller polls the ledger; create-work-order runs only on APPROVED.
Prove: nothing is written before approval.
simplified: Assembled from Service Bus, Functions and Tables. Logic Apps and Durable Functions are the managed alternatives and are not used here.
layers.native: Assembled pattern, not a single managed service.
layers.outcome: Writes that wait for a human, with a ledger of every decision

layers.title: Access and Perimeter
layers.objective: Sign users in, carry their identity to every layer, and put a protected edge in front of the tools.
learn: Identity provider, sign-in and tokens
Verify the token at the edge
A web firewall and rate limits
services: Front Door and Application Gateway WAF
build: Entra: register an app, create a client secret and a user.
Client-credentials token and user sign-in; the JWT verifies against the tenant signing keys (RS256).
APIM: service, API, operations, validate-jwt policy and a subscription.
A call without a subscription key is rejected.
Create the WAF policies.
checks: token verifies against the tenant keys
simplified: Tokens are real signed JWTs; Conditional Access, MFA and federation are simplified.
layers.outcome: Sign-in, a verified token and a protected API edge

layers.title: Channels and Input Guardrails
layers.objective: Let people reach the agent, filter what comes in, and tell approvers what is waiting.
learn: Input guardrails: prompt attacks and blocked terms
The approver inbox: a topic with a queue behind it
build: Content Safety analyze_text: a benign question is allowed and violent text is flagged.
Bind an RAI policy (facilities-guardrail) to a deployment: a violent prompt is refused with 400 content_filter.
A benign prompt reaches the model.
Create the Service Bus namespace, topic and approver-inbox subscription; send, receive and complete a message.
simplified: Content Safety is a deterministic filter set, not Microsoft's trained classifiers.
layers.outcome: Input guardrails and an approver inbox

layers.title: AgentOps and Observability
layers.objective: See what the agent did: a trace per step, metrics for KPIs, and structured logs tied to the trace.
learn: Spans per agent and per tool
Metrics and logs correlated by trace id
build: Create a Log Analytics workspace and a workspace-based Application Insights component.
Export one span per agent or tool step with azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter.
Export a structured log line and a custom metric (facilities.tool_calls).
Read the spans, log and metric back with KQL (azure-monitor-query).
Custom table ingest, then KQL summarize.
simplified: KQL support covers the queries the reference uses; alert rules and workbooks are not simulated.
layers.outcome: Traces, metrics and logs you can read back

layers.title: Governance and Security
layers.objective: Protect and audit the whole app: encrypt the sensitive records and prove who did what.
learn: Envelope protection with an encryption context
An audit trail of the run and the approval events
build: Create the vault facilities-kv through ARM.
Create the RSA key ledger-key with azure-keyvault-keys (needs an https vault URI).
Envelope encryption: wrap and unwrap a data key that protects a ledger record; encrypt and decrypt round trip.
Activity Log: the run's control-plane operations, filtered by resource group.
simplified: RBAC evaluation is simplified; check the capability notes for what is enforced.
layers.outcome: Encrypted records and an audit trail of the run
